sanskrit: prātar agniṃ prātar indraṃ havāmahe prātar mitrāvaruṇā prātar aśvinā | prātar bhagaṃ pūṣaṇaṃ brahmaṇaspatiṃ prātaḥ somam uta rudraṃ huvema ||
english: At dawn we invoke Agni, at dawn Indra, at dawn Mitra and Varuṇa, at dawn the Aśvins; at dawn may we invoke Bhaga and Pūṣan, Brahmaṇaspati, and at dawn Soma and Rudra.

sanskrit: prātarjitaṃ bhagam ugraṃ huvema vayaṃ putram aditer yo vidhartā | ādhraś cid yaṃ manyamānas turaś cid rājā cid yaṃ bhagaṃ bhakṣīty āha ||
english: We invoke fierce Bhaga, conqueror of the dawn, son of Aditi who is the apportioner; even the destitute man, though he be shrewd, and even a king says of him: 'May I partake of Bhaga's portion.'

sanskrit: bhaga praṇetar bhaga satyarādho bhagemāṃ dhiyam ud avā dadan naḥ | bhaga pra ṇo janaya gobhir aśvair bhaga pra nṛbhir nṛvantaḥ syāma ||
english: O Bhaga, leader, O Bhaga of true bounty — O Bhaga, uphold this prayer of ours, granting it; O Bhaga, generate for us cattle and horses; O Bhaga, may we be rich in men, with heroes.

sanskrit: utedānīṃ bhagavantaḥ syāma- -uta prapitva uta madhye ahnām | utodite maghavan sūrye vayaṃ devānāṃ sumatau syāma ||
english: May we be rich in Bhaga's blessing now, and at the departure of day, and in the middle of the day; and when the generous sun has risen, O Maghavan, may we be in the good graces of the gods.

sanskrit: bhaga eva bhagavām̐ astu devās tena vayaṃ bhagavantaḥ syāma | taṃ tvā bhaga sarva ij johavīti sa no bhaga puraetā bhaveha ||
english: May Bhaga himself be the blessed one among the gods; through him may we be blessed. All people call upon you, O Bhaga — be for us, O Bhaga, a forerunner here.

sanskrit: sam adhvarāyoṣaso namanta dadhikrāveva śucaye padāya | arvācīnaṃ vasuvidaṃ bhagaṃ no ratham ivāśvā vājina ā vahantu ||
english: The dawns bow together for the sacrifice, as Dadhikrāvan bows toward the bright track; may swift steeds carry toward us Bhaga who finds wealth, drawing him as horses draw a chariot.

sanskrit: aśvāvatīr gomatīr na uṣāso vīravatīḥ sadam ucchantu bhadrāḥ | ghṛtaṃ duhānā viśvataḥ prapītā yūyaṃ pāta svastibhiḥ sadā naḥ ||
english: May the auspicious dawns ever shine upon us, rich in horses, rich in cattle, rich in heroes; milking out ghee, drunk all around — do you always protect us with blessings.

sanskrit: yas te manyo 'vidhad vajra sāyaka saha ojaḥ puṣyati viśvam ānuṣak | sāhyāma dāsam āryaṃ tvayā yujā vayaṃ sahaskṛtena sahasā sahīyasā ||
english: O Manyu, that bolt of yours which was kindled as an arrow, which nourishes all power in succession — with you as our ally, O fashioner of strength, with might overcoming all, may we overcome the Dāsa and the Ārya.

sanskrit: manyur indro manyur evāsa devo manyur hotā varuṇo jātavedāḥ | manyur viśa īḍate mānuṣīr yāḥ pāhi no manyo tapasā sajoṣāḥ ||
english: Manyu is Indra, Manyu himself was the god; Manyu is the Hotṛ-priest, Varuṇa, Jātavedas; Manyu is besought by the human clans — protect us, O Manyu, with your ardor, united in goodwill.

sanskrit: abhīhi manyo tavasas tavīyān tapasā yujā vi jahi śatrūn | amitrahā vṛtrahā dasyuhā ca viśvā vasūny ā bharā tvaṃ naḥ ||
english: Come forward, O Manyu, mightier than the mighty; with ardor as your ally, smite the enemies asunder; slayer of foes, slayer of Vṛtra, slayer of Dasyus — bring to us all treasures.

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi manyo abhibhūtyojāḥ svayambhūr bhāmo abhimātiṣāhaḥ | viśvacarṣaṇiḥ sahuriḥ sahīyām̐ asmāsv ojaḥ pṛtanāsu dhehi ||
english: For you, O Manyu, are of overpowering might, self-born, radiant, conqueror of the arrogant, ranging over all peoples, overpowering, the mightier of the mighty — place your vigor in us in battles.

sanskrit: abhāgaḥ sann apa pareto asmi tava kratvā taviṣasya pracetaḥ | taṃ tvā manyo akratur jihīḍāhaṃ svā tanūr baladāvā na ehi ||
english: Without a share and exiled as I am, O discerning one, through your will of the mighty — I, the impotent one, have irritated you, O Manyu; come to me yourself as a strength-giver, my own body's ally.

sanskrit: ayaṃ te asmy upa na ehy arvāṅ pratīcīnaḥ sahure viśvadāvan | manyo vajrinn upa na ā vavṛtsva hanāva dasyūṃr uta bodhy āpe ||
english: I am yours — come here facing me, O overpowering one, giver of all; O Manyu, bearer of the thunderbolt, turn back toward us; may we smite the Dasyus and be awake to the waters.

sanskrit: abhi prehi dakṣiṇato bhavā no adhā vṛtrāṇi jaṅghanāva bhūri | juhomi te dharuṇo madhvo agram ubhā upāṃśu prathamā pibeva ||
english: March forward, be to us on the right side; then may we smite enemies abundantly; I pour for you the first drop of the sustaining sweet drink — let us two drink together in a whisper, as the first.

sanskrit: agner manve prathamasya pracetasaḥ pāñcajanyasya bahudhā yam indhate | viśoviśaḥ praviśivāṃsam īmahe sa no muñcatv aṃhasaḥ ||
english: I reflect on Agni, the first, the discerning, Pāñcajanya, whom the people kindle in many ways; we supplicate him who has entered each and every clan — may he release us from distress.

sanskrit: sujātaṃ jātavedasam agniṃ vaiśvānaraṃ vibhum | havyavāhaṃ havāmahe sa no muñcatv aṃhasaḥ ||
english: We invoke well-born Jātavedas, Agni Vaiśvānara, the all-pervading, the carrier of oblations — may he release us from distress.

sanskrit: yathā havyaṃ vahasi jātavedo yathā yajñaṃ kalpayasi prajānan | evā devebhyaḥ sumatim ihā vaha sa no muñcatv aṃhasaḥ ||
english: As you carry the oblation, O Jātavedas, as you arrange the sacrifice in your wisdom — so bring here right-mindedness for the gods; may he release us from distress.

sanskrit: yāmanyāmann upayuktaṃ vahiṣṭhaṃ karmankarmann ābhagam | agnim īḍe rakṣohaṇaṃ yajñavṛdhaṃ ghṛtāhutaṃ sa no muñcatv aṃhasaḥ ||
english: In every journey, the best carrier for the work; in every ritual act, the one taking his due share — I praise Agni, slayer of demons, increaser of sacrifice, fed with ghee; may he release us from distress.

sanskrit: yena rṣayo valam adyotayan yujā yenāsurāṇām ayuvanta māyāḥ | yenāgninā paṇīn indro jigāya sa no muñcatv aṃhasaḥ ||
english: He with whom as ally the ṛṣis shone apart Vala, through whom the sorceries of the Asuras were cut away, that Agni with whom Indra conquered the Paṇis — may he release us from distress.

sanskrit: yena devā amṛtam anvavindan yenauṣadhīr madhumatīr akṛṇvan | yenedaṃ svar ābharan sa no muñcatv aṃhasaḥ ||
english: He through whom the gods found the immortal draught, through whom they made the herbs honey-sweet, through whom they brought forth this heavenly light — may he release us from distress.

sanskrit: yasyedaṃ pradiśi yad virocate yaj jātaṃ janitavyaṃ ca kevalam | staumy agniṃ nāthito johavīmi sa no muñcatv aṃhasaḥ ||
english: In whose direction all this shines forth, whatever has been born and whatever is yet to be born in its entirety — I praise Agni, being in need I call him repeatedly; may he release us from distress.
